title: What safety training must private sector employers give workers under UAE federal labor law?
seoTitle: UAE labor law safety training duties
description: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 and Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022: employer duties to inform, instruct and train workers on safety risks.
shortAnswer: Article 13(6) of UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 requires private sector employers to provide prevention measures, guidance and awareness, and appropriate training so workers avoid occupational injury and disease risks. Article 22 of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022 adds that workers must be told the risks of their job before starting, with written instructions in Arabic and a language they understand. Breaches can be fined AED 5,000 to AED 1,000,000 per worker affected.
keyTakeaways: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 on the Regulation of Labor Relations has applied to private sector employers since February 2, 2022; article 13(6) is the core safety training duty.

Article 22(1) of the Executive Regulation (Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022) requires employers to inform workers of job risks before handing over work and to post detailed safety instructions in Arabic and another language workers understand.

Article 23(3) of the Executive Regulation links training to injury compensation: an employer can deny compensation for a deliberate safety breach only if it informed, trained and educated the worker as specified.
Establishments with 50 or more workers must set work regulations that include precautions against work injuries and fire hazards (Executive Regulation article 14).
General violations carry a fine of AED 5,000 to AED 1,000,000 (article 63), multiplied by the number of workers affected up to AED 10,000,000 (article 62).
regulator: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE), coordinating with federal and emirate occupational health and safety authorities
appliesTo: Private sector establishments and employers across the UAE that are subject to Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021
Supervisors who hand over work and must brief workers on its risks
HR and HSE teams that maintain work regulations, safety instructions and training records
Employers of juveniles, who must train them on using safety and health equipment

sections.heading: Which federal laws set safety training duties for UAE private sector employers?

blocks.text: Two federal instruments set the baseline. Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 Regulating Labor Relations (المرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم 33 لسنة 2021 بشأن تنظيم علاقات العمل) was issued on September 20, 2021, published in Official Gazette No. 712 (supplement) on September 26, 2021, and took effect on February 2, 2022 ([UAE Legislations: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1541)). Its Executive Regulation is Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022 ([UAE Legislations: Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1547)).

Article 3 applies the Decree-Law to all establishments, employers and workers in the private sector, excluding federal and local government employees, the armed forces, police and security, and domestic workers. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) administers it. The UAE Government portal also points employers to Ministerial Resolution No. 44 of 2022 and Administrative Decision No. 19 of 2023 on occupational safety and health and labor accommodation ([u.ae: health and safety at the workplace](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/jobs/Workplace-regulations/health-and-safety-at-workplace)).

blocks.title: Federal baseline and emirate frameworks
blocks.text: Emirate level systems add detail on top of the federal baseline. In Abu Dhabi, for example, the occupational safety and health system framework sets risk based training procedures, covered in [Abu Dhabi's OSHAD framework](/regulations/oshad-abu-dhabi-ohs-training). This page covers only the federal labor law duties, as at November 2026. The official English texts state that the Arabic text prevails in case of conflict.

sections.heading: What does article 13 of the Decree-Law require employers to do about training?

blocks.text: Article 13(6) is the central duty. In the official English translation, the employer must "Provide the necessary means of prevention to protect Workers from the dangers of occupational injuries and diseases that may occur during work, ensure the provision of guidance and awareness regulations, provide appropriate training for workers to avoid such risks, and conduct periodic evaluation to ensure that all work parties comply with the requirements of health and occupational safety and security" ([Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, English text](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1541/download)).

items: **Article 13(5):** invest in developing workers' skills and provide a minimum of training and qualification programs and tools, under the Decree-Law and its Executive Regulation.
**Article 13(7):** take what is necessary to ensure each worker knows their rights and obligations at work, using tools and methods suited to the work and the workforce.
**Article 16(6):** the worker must implement the occupational safety and health instructions determined in the establishment.

**Article 36:** establishments must comply with Federal Law No. 13 of 2020 on Public Health, and the Executive Regulation defines MoHRE's role and the rules on workers' safety, protection and health care.

blocks.text: The Decree-Law does not prescribe hours, curricula or refresher intervals. The duty is outcome based: training must be "appropriate" to the risks, and the employer must periodically evaluate compliance. That makes a documented risk based training plan, of the kind described in [how to map training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations), the most practical way to show the duty is met.

sections.heading: What does the Executive Regulation add on instruction before work?

blocks.text: Article 22 of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022, titled Workers' Safety, Protection and Health Care, turns the general duty into specific actions ([Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022, English text](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1547/download)). Under article 22(1), every employer must:

items: Provide adequate prevention means against occupational injuries and illnesses, fire hazards and risks from machines and work tools, and follow any other prevention methods MoHRE determines (a).

Post in a prominent place detailed, clear instructions on fire prevention, protection from the risks of the work and how to treat resulting accidents, in Arabic and in another language the workers understand when needed, with warning signs at dangerous spots (b).
Inform workers, before handing over the work, of the risks of their profession, such as fire, machines, falls and occupational illnesses (c).
Assign supervision of first aid to a specialist and stock each first aid box (d).

Take continuous practical measures to prevent, reduce or eliminate health hazards and protect against falls, falling objects, chemicals, hot or flammable substances, compressed gases and electricity (f to h).
Hang guiding boards at machinery and operations showing the necessary technical instructions in Arabic and another language workers understand when needed (i).

blocks.text: Article 22(2) requires workers to use the protective equipment provided and follow safety instructions, and lets the employer apply its list of sanctions to workers who breach them. Article 22(3) gives MoHRE the role of coordinating with health and safety authorities, inspecting establishments and imposing administrative penalties for breaches of occupational health and safety instructions.

sections.heading: How does safety training affect work injury compensation?

blocks.text: Training records decide whether an employer can rely on a worker's deliberate safety breach to refuse compensation. Article 23(3) of the Executive Regulation states that a worker is not entitled to compensation if the injury resulted from a deliberate violation of posted precautionary instructions, provided the employer met four conditions.

blocks.caption: The four employer conditions in article 23(3) of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022
head: Condition
What the employer must have done
Evidence that proves it
rows: (a) Awareness
Made workers aware of detailed fire prevention and hazard protection instructions, in Arabic and another language workers understand when needed
Posted instructions with languages shown; acknowledgment records
(b) Pre work briefing and PPE
Informed the worker of the job's risks before work, required use of prevention means, supplied personal protective tools and trained the worker to use them
Dated pre task briefing record; PPE issue log; PPE training record
(c) Safety training
Trained the worker on the safety means set out in the workers' protection instructions
Training record mapped to the establishment's protection instructions
(d) Education on hiring
Educated the worker on hiring about the risks of the job and the prevention means to follow, and hung written instructions in the workplace
Induction record listing job risks covered; photo or register of posted instructions

blocks.text: Without that evidence, the defense is unavailable and the ordinary compensation rules apply. The UAE Government portal notes that death compensation equals 24 months of basic wage, between AED 18,000 and AED 200,000, under Cabinet Resolution No. 33 of 2022 and the Decree-Law.

sections.heading: What extra duties apply to larger establishments and to juvenile workers?

blocks.text: Establishments with 50 or more workers must set written work regulations, including a list of work instructions that covers the measures and precautions needed to avoid work injuries and fire hazards (Executive Regulation article 14(3)). According to the UAE Government portal, establishments of that size must also run a system for monitoring work injuries and occupational diseases that includes preventive tools and training programs for workers in high risk activities, an inventory of dangerous activities, and a record of workers exposed to occupational hazards kept for at least five years after their service ends.

For juveniles, article 4(3)(c) of the Executive Regulation requires an employer employing a juvenile to train them on how to use safety and occupational health equipment, alongside keeping a special juvenile register and providing insurance. Article 4(1) prohibits employing juveniles in hazardous or harmful jobs.

sections.heading: What are the penalties and employment consequences of safety training failures?

blocks.text: Failing to meet these duties falls under the general penalty in article 63 of the Decree-Law: a fine of AED 5,000 to AED 1,000,000 for violating any other provision of the Decree-Law, its Executive Regulation or implementing resolutions. Article 62 multiplies fines by the number of workers affected, up to AED 10,000,000, and article 64 provides for imprisonment or double fines for repeat violations within a year.

items: **Dismissal without notice (article 44(3)):** an employer may dismiss a worker who violates the establishment's safety instructions, but only if the instructions are written, displayed in a visible place and the worker has been informed of them.

**Leaving without notice (article 45(3)):** a worker may leave without notice if there is a grave danger at the workplace that threatens their safety or health, the employer knew of it, and the employer took no measures to remove it.

blocks.text: Both provisions reward documented communication. An employer that cannot show a worker was informed of written, displayed instructions cannot use article 44(3), so the induction record and the posted instruction register are as important as the training itself.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each risk in an establishment's protection instructions to the roles exposed, the pre work briefing, the PPE training and the language of delivery, so the four article 23(3) conditions can be evidenced from one framework. When work instructions change, the affected briefings and posted materials are traced rather than rediscovered.

faqs.q: Does UAE federal labor law set minimum hours for safety training?
faqs.a: No. Article 13(6) of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 requires appropriate training to avoid occupational risks, and the Executive Regulation specifies what workers must be told and trained on, but neither sets hours or refresher intervals. Emirate frameworks and sector regulators may add more specific requirements.

faqs.q: Must safety instructions be in Arabic in the UAE?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 22(1)(b) and (i) of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022 require posted safety instructions and machinery guidance boards in Arabic, and in another language the workers understand when needed. Article 23(3)(a) repeats the language requirement for awareness of protection instructions.

faqs.q: Does the federal labor law apply to domestic workers and government employees?
faqs.a: No. Article 3 excludes federal and local government employees, members of the armed forces, police and security, and domestic workers, who are covered by separate legislation. The Cabinet may also exclude other categories on the Minister's proposal.

faqs.q: How quickly must a workplace injury be reported to MoHRE?
faqs.a: According to the UAE Government portal, in the case of an injury or death at the workplace the employer must inform MoHRE within 48 hours of the incident, through the MoHRE website, approved business service centers, the MoHRE app or other specified channels.
